- If sentiment shows strong positive bias (e.g., >0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment shows strong negative bias (e.g., < -0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply downward correction by 5–15% of peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after a rally), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model tends to be overly optimistic; apply a 3–7% downward bias to forecast.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 30d), consider reducing baseline by 2–5% for next forecast horizon.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to pivot; adjust forecast mid-period to reflect sentiment reversal.
